body: I can confirm the issue, it's a regression from 4.7 dev 2. I can't reproduce with a self compiled build with `dev_build=yes scu_build=yes arch=x86_32`, so probably some optimaztion that don't play well with 32 bits version. Attempt to compile optimized versions (`production=yes`) results in an error while compiling so i can't investigate futher.

I can reproduce this with the 4.7.1.stable official x86_32 binary (which is compiled with MinGW).

I bisected the regression to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/115877. cc @mihe @jrouwe 

When compiling 5902d3f37 locally with MSVC 2022 (tested 17.14.13 and 17.14.37) and `arch=x86_32 optimize=none` or `optimize=debug`, I can't reproduce the issue.

Ok, I figured out what the issue is. Basically MinGW32 lies that `__STDCPP_DEFAULT_NEW_ALIGNMENT__ == 16` but its allocations are actually 8 byte aligned. This can be verified by compiling and running the following program:

```C++
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <new>

int main(int, char **)
{
	printf("malloc\n");
	for (int i = 0; i < 100; ++i)
	{
	   void *d = malloc(4);
	   printf("%p\n", d);
	}

	printf("new\n");
	for (int i = 0; i < 100; ++i)
	{
	   int *d = new int();
	   printf("%p\n", d);
	}

	printf("%d", __STDCPP_DEFAULT_NEW_ALIGNMENT__);
	return 1;
}
```

so you see that both `new` and `malloc` return 8 byte aligned blocks. 

Since 5.5.0 Jolt uses `JPH_DEFAULT_ALLOCATE_ALIGNMENT` (which defaults to `__STDCPP_DEFAULT_NEW_ALIGNMENT__`) to decide wether or not to use aligned allocations for arrays. On MinGW32 this leads to `TriangleSplitterBinning::mBins` not being 16 byte aligned. This causes an unaligned `__m128` read which triggers this crash.

Note that I fixed a variant of this in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/105455#issuecomment-2824311547. I'll create a patch for this similar to last time.
